source.title: Piano Syllabus, 2022 Edition (The Royal Conservatory of Music, RCM Certificate Program)
source.meaning: RCM Piano Syllabus levels (Preparatory A, Preparatory B, Levels 1-10) are examination requirements per level: each level lists the technical tests, ear tests and sight-reading tests a candidate is examined on at that level (plus etudes and repertoire, which are not extracted here).
source.pageNumbering: All 'page' values are PDF page numbers; they equal the printed page numbers in this document.

notes: Accidental signs (flat/sharp) are missing from pdftotext output ('B major' for B-flat major). Every key list here was read by eye from page images (130 dpi full-page views); entries carry keysReadFrom:'page image'. Level 10 spot-checked at 240 dpi.
Tempo cells: the pdftotext output keeps only '= N'; the note glyph before '=' was read by eye as a crotchet in every cell (unit:'crotchet', unitReadFrom:'page image').

Note-value / rest-value glyph cells (technical-test 'Note Values' column; ear-test and sight-reading 'Note Values' and 'Time Signature(s)' cells) have no text; they were read by eye and are marked readFrom:'page image'. Descriptions use British note names and describe shapes only. Time-signature glyphs (stacked digits) were read at 240 dpi crops for Levels 1-7 musicianship tables, Level 8-9 and Level 5-6 tables; the other time-signature cells (Preparatory A/B, Level 10, Level 8 lead-sheet, Level 9 playing/lead-sheet) were read from 130 dpi page views and are marked resolution:'130 dpi view'.

Beam counts in groups of four beamed notes: Level 6 technical-test cells were checked at 240 dpi and show a double beam (semiquavers). In Levels 7-10 the same-looking group renders with what looks like more beams at 240 dpi (Level 7 crop) but the beam count could not be reliably resolved; those cells are described as 'group of four beamed notes' with uncertain:true and no rhythmic value is asserted.
Preparatory A and B 'Playing' tasks print a staff showing the allowed starting notes and fingerings; that music notation was not transcribed: {unread} entries mark it. Page must be read by eye.

The ear-test 'Chord Progressions' formula in Levels 8-10 uses figured-bass numerals (superscript/subscript); read by eye from 240 dpi crops (Levels 8, 9, 10): 'I-IV-V 6-5 over 4-3 -I' (Level 8) and 'I-VI-IV-V 6 over 4 - V 8-7 -I' (Levels 9, 10). The en-dash separated figures are reproduced as printed.

Level 10 minor keys printed for the four-octave scales are 'F-sharp, G, G-sharp, A, B-flat, B minor' but for the tonic four-note chords 'F-sharp, G, A-flat, A, B-flat, B minor'; both read at 240 dpi and kept as printed (G-sharp vs A-flat difference may be intentional or an inconsistency in the source).

Levels 9 and 10 repeat the sight-playing section on the page after the musicianship page (Level 9: p. 82; Level 10: p. 93). Level 8 technical tests are on p. 70 and the musicianship page on p. 71; Level 1-7 technical tests and musicianship are on consecutive pages as cited per entry.

Etudes, repertoire lists, Theory prerequisites and the diploma levels are not extracted. 'HS' = hands separately and 'HT' = hands together, as printed (the abbreviations are not expanded in the source on the cited pages; the expansion is the common reading and is flagged here, not a printed definition).

Chord formulae and chord-name lists use a plain hyphen where the source prints an en dash (e.g. I-IV-I for I–IV–I; major-minor 7th); accidentals are spelled out (B-flat, F-sharp). Task sentences are quoted from the page text but several lines were rejoined; where a sentence begins OR/AND it is the source's own italic connector.
Technical-test cells that span several rows (e.g. a single 'Played' cell shared by a broken row and a solid/blocked row) are recorded on each row with sharedCell:true.

keys.value: major and minor keys up to five sharps or flats

alternativeLeadSheet.value: Students may choose to read a lead sheet (with a melody and root/quality chord symbols) and realize an accompaniment based on the chord symbols provided. Harmonic vocabulary will be aligned with the chords presented for study in Level 9 Harmony in the Theory Syllabus. Students are expected to provide creative accompaniments appropriate to the style of the given melody.

task.value: Students will be asked to identify any of the following intervals. The examiner will play each interval in melodic form (ascending or descending) followed by harmonic form once.

alternative.value: OR Students may choose to sing or hum any of the following intervals (ascending or descending). The examiner will play the first note once.

task.value: Students will be asked to identify the quality of the following chords after the examiner has played the chord in solid/blocked form, close position once.

value: major and minor four-note chords (root position, 1st inversion)

task.value: Students will be asked to identify each chord in a four-chord progression in a major or minor key after the examiner has played the progression twice. In the second playing, the examiner will pause on each chord for the student to identify it. The progression will be played in keyboard style, beginning on the tonic chord, and may include any of the following chords.

value.major: I, IV, V, vi (root position only)
value.minor: i, iv, V, VI (root position only)

task.value: Students will be asked to play back the upper part of a two-part phrase. The examiner will identify the key and time signature, play the tonic chord once, and play the phrase three times. Before the first playing, the examiner will count one measure. After the second playing, the student will clap the rhythm or sing the upper part of the phrase. After the third playing, the student will play the upper part of the phrase.

keys.value: any major or minor key, up to four sharps or flats

task.value: Students may choose to play back a two-measure opening, complete the question (antecedent) phrase, and improvise an answer (consequent) phrase to create an eight-measure contrasting period. The examiner will identify the key and time signature, play the tonic chord once, and play the two-measure opening three times.
